questions.question: A point charge of +4 μC is placed in vacuum. The electric potential at a distance of 0.3 m from it is approximately: (k = 9×10⁹ N·m²/C²)
Two identical point charges repel each other with a force of 0.1 N when placed 0.3 m apart in vacuum. The magnitude of each charge is: (k = 9×10⁹ N·m²/C²)
The electric flux through a closed surface enclosing a net charge of 2 μC is approximately: (ε₀ = 8.85×10⁻¹² C²/N·m²)
questions.explanation: By Gauss's law, Φ = q/ε₀ = 2×10⁻⁶/8.85×10⁻¹² ≈ 2.26×10⁵ N·m²/C.

questions.question: A parallel plate capacitor has plate area 0.05 m² and separation 1 mm. When a dielectric slab of constant K is inserted, the capacitance becomes 177 pF. The value of K is: (ε₀ = 8.85×10⁻¹² F/m)
A dipole consists of charges +5 nC and -5 nC separated by 2 mm. It is placed in a uniform electric field of 10⁴ N/C at an angle of 60°. The torque on the dipole is approximately:
Three charges +q, +2q, and +3q are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side a. The total electrostatic potential energy of the system is: (k = 1/4πε₀)
A resistor of 20 Ω carries a current of 0.5 A. The power dissipated in the resistor is:
A 100 W, 220 V bulb is operated at rated voltage. Its resistance is:
In a Wheatstone bridge, P = 5 Ω, Q = 10 Ω, R = 15 Ω. For balance, S should be:
questions.explanation: For balance, P/Q = R/S → 5/10 = 15/S → S = 30 Ω.

questions.question: A battery of emf 9 V and internal resistance 1 Ω is connected to an external resistor of 2 Ω. The current in the circuit is:
A wire of resistivity 2.8×10⁻⁸ Ω·m has length 5 m and cross-sectional area 1 mm². Its resistance is:
Two batteries of emf 6 V (internal resistance 1 Ω) and 12 V (internal resistance 2 Ω) are connected in parallel (like terminals together). The terminal voltage across the combination is:
questions.explanation: For parallel batteries: V = (E₁/r₁ + E₂/r₂)/(1/r₁ + 1/r₂) = (6/1 + 12/2)/(1/1 + 1/2) = (6+6)/1.5 = 8 V.

questions.topic: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.question: A straight wire carries a current of 3 A. The magnetic field at a point 5 cm from the wire is: (μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ T·m/A)

questions.topic: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.question: A circular loop of radius 0.2 m carries a current of 5 A. The magnetic field at its center is: (μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ T·m/A)

questions.topic: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.question: A charged particle of mass m and charge q moves perpendicular to a magnetic field B with speed v. The frequency of its circular motion is:
questions.explanation: For circular motion in a magnetic field, mv²/r = qvB → ω = v/r = qB/m. Frequency f = ω/(2π) = qB/(2πm).

questions.topic: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.question: A bar magnet of pole strength 20 A·m and length 0.1 m is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.3 T at an angle of 60°. The torque on it is approximately:
questions.explanation: Magnetic moment m = pole strength × length = 20×0.1 = 2 A·m². τ = mB sinθ = 2×0.3×sin60° = 0.52 N·m.

questions.topic: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.question: A current of 4 A flows through a circular coil of radius 0.1 m with 20 turns. The magnetic field at the center of the coil is: (μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ T·m/A)

questions.topic: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.question: Two parallel wires carrying currents of 2 A and 4 A in opposite directions are separated by 10 cm. The force per unit length between them is: (μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ T·m/A)
questions.explanation: F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd) = (4π×10⁻⁷×2×4)/(2π×0.1) = 1.6×10⁻⁵ N/m. Opposite currents repel each other.

questions.question: The induced emf in a coil of 50 turns when the magnetic flux changes from 0.1 Wb to 0.4 Wb in 0.2 s is:
In a pure capacitive AC circuit, the current:
options: C) Is in phase with voltage
questions.explanation: In a pure capacitive AC circuit, the current leads the voltage by π/2 (90°) because charge accumulation on plates causes current to flow before voltage builds up.

questions.question: A series LCR circuit has R = 15 Ω, X_L = 25 Ω, and X_C = 15 Ω. The impedance is approximately:
An ideal transformer has 400 turns in primary and 100 turns in secondary. If primary is connected to 200 V AC and secondary feeds a 25 Ω load, the primary current is:
A series LCR circuit with R = 5 Ω, L = 0.5 H, and C = 20 μF resonates at angular frequency ω₀. The quality factor Q of the circuit is:
A series LCR circuit has L = 0.2 H and C = 5 μF. The resonant angular frequency and quality factor (R = 10 Ω) are respectively:
The speed of electromagnetic waves in a medium with relative permittivity 9 and relative permeability 1 is:
In an electromagnetic wave, the electric field is E = E₀ cos(kx - ωt). The corresponding magnetic field is:
questions.explanation: In an EM wave, E and B oscillate in phase. If E = E₀ cos(kx - ωt), then B = B₀ cos(kx - ωt) with E₀/B₀ = c.

questions.question: Which electromagnetic wave is commonly used for sterilization of medical equipment?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation is used for sterilization because it has enough energy to damage the DNA of microorganisms.

questions.question: The amplitude of electric field in an electromagnetic wave is 6 V/m. The amplitude of magnetic field is: (c = 3×10⁸ m/s)
An electromagnetic wave of intensity 1000 W/m² is incident on a perfectly reflecting surface. The radiation pressure is approximately: (c = 3×10⁸ m/s)
questions.explanation: For a perfectly reflecting surface, P = 2I/c = 2×1000/(3×10⁸) = 6.67×10⁻⁶ Pa.

questions.question: A convex lens of focal length 15 cm forms an image of an object placed 30 cm away. The image distance is:
A concave mirror has a focal length of 20 cm. An object is placed 40 cm in front of it. The image is formed at:
options: B) 40 cm in front of mirror
C) 20 cm in front of mirror

questions.question: Light passes from water (n=1.33) to air. The critical angle is approximately:
A convex lens of focal length 20 cm and a concave lens of focal length 30 cm are placed in contact. The focal length of the combination is:
In Young's double slit experiment, the distance between the slits is 0.5 mm and the screen is 1.5 m away. If the fringe width is 1.5 mm, the wavelength of light used is:
A telescope has an objective of focal length 80 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 4 cm. When focused on a distant object with the final image at infinity, the separation between the lenses is:
questions.explanation: For relaxed eye (image at infinity), lens separation L = f₀ + fₑ = 80 + 4 = 84 cm.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.question: The energy of a photon of frequency 6×10¹⁴ Hz is approximately: (h = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ J·s)

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.question: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of incident light (frequency above threshold) increases:
options: A) The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons
D) The number of photoelectrons emitted
questions.explanation: Intensity affects the number of photons, hence the number of photoelectrons. The maximum kinetic energy depends only on frequency, not intensity.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.question: The work function of a metal is 3.5 eV. The threshold wavelength for this metal is approximately: (hc ≈ 1240 eV·nm)

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.question: An electron is accelerated through 200 V. Its de-Broglie wavelength is approximately:

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.question: Light of wavelength 250 nm is incident on a metal with work function 4 eV. The maximum speed of emitted electrons is approximately: (h = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 3×10⁸ m/s, mₑ = 9.1×10⁻³¹ kg)
In the Bohr model of hydrogen, the angular momentum of the electron in the second orbit (n=2) is:
questions.explanation: L = nh/2π. For n=2: L = 2h/2π = h/π.

questions.question: The binding energy per nucleon is maximum for which element?
questions.explanation: The binding energy per nucleon peaks around iron (⁵⁶Fe), making it the most stable nucleus.

questions.question: A radioactive sample has 8000 nuclei and a half-life of 2 days. The number of nuclei remaining after 6 days is:

The energy released in the fusion reaction ²H + ³H → ⁴He + n is approximately 17.6 MeV. If 2 kg of deuterium undergoes fusion, the total energy released is approximately: (N_A = 6.02×10²³, 1 MeV = 1.6×10⁻¹³ J)
In a hydrogen-like atom with Z=2 (singly ionized helium), the wavelength of radiation emitted when an electron transitions from n=3 to n=2 is approximately: (R = 1.097×10⁷ m⁻¹)
The number of valence electrons in a silicon atom is:
questions.explanation: Silicon (atomic number 14) is in group 14 of the periodic table and has 4 valence electrons.

questions.question: In a half-wave rectifier circuit, the output voltage waveform consists of:
options: A) Both positive and negative half-cycles
questions.explanation: A half-wave rectifier passes only one half-cycle (either positive or negative depending on diode orientation) of the input AC, blocking the other.

questions.question: In a common-emitter transistor amplifier, the phase difference between input and output voltages is:
questions.explanation: In a common-emitter configuration, the output voltage is inverted with respect to the input, giving a phase difference of 180°.

questions.question: A logic circuit has two inputs A and B, and one output Y. The output is HIGH when at least one input is HIGH. This is an:
questions.explanation: An OR gate outputs HIGH when at least one input is HIGH. Its truth table matches the description.

questions.question: In a full-wave bridge rectifier, if the input AC has a peak voltage of 50 V, the average DC output voltage is approximately:
